questions.title: What is Critical Rendering Path and how does the browser render a page?
questions.description:
Critical Rendering Path (CRP)

The Critical Rendering Path is the sequence of steps the browser goes through to convert HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into actual pixels on the screen.

The Steps

  1. DOM Construction: Parse HTML to build the Document Object Model tree.
  2. CSSOM Construction: Parse CSS to build the CSS Object Model tree.
  3. Render Tree: Combine DOM and CSSOM (filtering out hidden nodes like display: none).
  4. Layout (Reflow): Calculate exact sizes and positions of each node.
  5. Paint: Fill in pixels (colors, borders, images).
  6. Composite: Layer the painted elements together for display.
questions.bestPractices:
• Minimize render-blocking assets (critical CSS, async/defer JS).
  • Avoid layout thrashing by grouping DOM reads and writes.
questions.commonMistakes: • Placing large synchronous scripts in the <head>, which halts DOM construction until the script is downloaded and executed.
questions.example:
<!-- BAD: Blocks DOM parsing -->
<script src="heavy.js"></script>

<!-- GOOD: Non-blocking -->
<script src="heavy.js" defer></script>
<script src="tracker.js" async></script>
questions.interviewTip: Differentiate between async and defer. async runs as soon as it downloads (blocking HTML parsing), while defer preserves script order and runs only after DOM parsing finishes.
